title: How He Left Corporate Law to Build $7K/Month in Vending Revenue
excerpt: A young law-school graduate walked away from investment banking compliance work to build a vending route doing close to $7K a month within a year.
quote: Although it's scary and there's a lot of risk involved, you're the one that's in control of your own journey.
body:
## Background

Evan Tomahong went to law school in San Diego before moving back home to Wisconsin, where he did compliance work in financial services and investment banking. He then took a break from the corporate world and was caddying full-time while figuring out his next step. He found Mike Hoffman on Twitter and joined Vendingpreneurs in December 2024, later shadowing Anthony on live installs in February 2025.

> I come from a legal background, went to law school out in San Diego. I'm from Wisconsin, so moved back home and then did some compliance work in the financial services, investment banking world.

## The Challenge

Leaving a prestige career track for an unproven business was a real risk, and it took months with nothing to show before his first location went in.

> I didn't get my first placement installed until June of 2025. If I joined December of '24, it took months and months to be able to get my first placement. There's always doubts, is this really the path that I want to go on?

## The Turning Point

Evan wanted ownership over his own career trajectory rather than letting a company determine it, and the community sped up his learning curve, including hands-on time shadowing installs.

> I need to take a little bit more ownership into my own hands of building something instead of having a company determine my career trajectory. I really wanted to own that and have a little bit more control over that trajectory.

## Where They Are Now

Evan's first placement went in June 2025. By Q3 2025 he was generating close to $7,000 every month, with growth projected into 2026. His highest-earning location does about $2,700 a month, and he is working to push it past $3,000 through pricing and product changes. He deliberately scaled slowly to keep service quality high and is building a small team.

> Close to 7,000 every single month in Q3, and we're projected to grow in 2026.
